newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia faces insurance phone sales future - expert.
newsitem.headline: Asia faces insurance phone sales future - expert.

text.p: Direct telephone and computer-based insurance sales will become dominant in Asia in the next five to 10 years, a senior industry figure told Reuters on Wednesday.

David Luckly, underwriting manager of Hong Kong's Union Insurance, predicted that direct selling techniques would be part of a sweeping revolution in insurance services in the region brought about by developments in information technology.
The pattern could follow the experience of the U.S. and Europe, where telephone-based insurers have secured massive market shares in motor and other personal lines insurances.

The UK's Direct Line, a part of Royal Bank of Scotland, is perhaps the best known example of the rapid rise of direct insurers. It has become the UK's biggest private car insurer in the last ten years, with 2.2 million motor policies in force in May.

Luckly had earlier told delegates at the East Asian Insurance Congress conference in Singapore that communications technology will "fundamentally change the way insurance business is carried on in a future which is much closer than many of us may believe."

Luckly said the relentless pace of technological change will "kill off the traditional insurance company competencies" to be replaced by information technology (IT) and communications-based skills sets.

It will also stoke competitive pressures in the market place as consumers demand ever-more sophisticated insurance products faster and insurers rush to respond to the needs of an affluent middle-class as it expands throughout Asia, he added.
Luckly made an analogy with the computer industry which today generates 70 percent of revenues from products that hit the market less than two years ago.
"The evidence suggests that the vast majority of quantum leaps in business performance are the direct result of IT investment," he said.
